data.why: the repo already bundles the IASC set203 practice dataset (4 same-field FITS frames ~21 min apart) that the README's own results table is built on; the /detect upload form expects exactly this kind of multi-frame FITS set.

goals: Upload a set of same-field telescope FITS frames and run the automated pipeline to detect candidate moving objects.
Review detected candidates' tracked positions and speeds, and see which are cross-matched to known cataloged asteroids.
Use the 'hunt by ear' sonification tool to roam the stacked image by keyboard and listen for movers too faint for single-frame detection.
Mark and confirm a hunt-by-ear candidate frame-by-frame, then review the blink comparator and spoken summary of the hunting session.
Open a named asteroid's 3D orbit viewer and read its hazard assessment (MOID, NASA Sentry impact probability).
Start a multi-observer orbit-fitting campaign, submit RA/Dec astrometric observations, and inspect the resulting Gauss-method orbit fit.

review.summary: The tree captures the tool's two ways of finding asteroids (pipeline and sonified shift-and-stack hunt) plus its triage, orbit-viewer and campaign extras, with honest labels and screens that match. The phase order buries the main purpose, some README-stated pieces are missing (tune mode, catalog identification with MOID, orbit-fit result), and the core hunt-by-ear tasks were never replayed by the second agent, so it needs fixes before filing.
